note: Every programme line here maps to curriculum NET actually teaches: the Ecogreen primary pacing guides (grades 1-5) and the secondary guide (grades 6-9) carried in the house curriculum data, plus the in-house lesson academies and the IELTS/business tracks the coach has taught. Nothing here is a made-up course name.

programmes.name: Early Years
programmes.format: Play-led, in-home or at your school
programmes.books: None — songs, story, movement and naming
programmes.blurb: A child this age cannot be taught grammar and does not need to be. This track builds the ear: the sounds, the rhythm, and the fact that another language is a normal thing to hear in your own living room.
does: Listening first — the 60% rule at its purest: mostly-understood input, repeated
Phonics groundwork: the 42 core sounds of UK Jolly Phonics, used to fix Vietnamese phonetic interference early
Naming games, action songs, and story time in English
Zero correction of errors inside a sentence — the target is willingness, not accuracy
programmes.outcome: By the end of the year: follows simple instructions in English, names the world around them, and never flinches when English is spoken.

programmes.name: Primary
programmes.cadence: 2 × 60 min / week, plus the 45/15 at home
programmes.books: Look · Global Success · Cambridge Primary Science · Cambridge
programmes.blurb: This is the track that keeps a child ahead of the school pacing guide instead of chasing it. NET teaches from the guides the schools actually use — Look and Global Success for English, Cambridge for Science — so the private hour reinforces the classroom week rather than competing with it.
does: The 10-5-5-3 anatomy: 10 words in real sentences, 5 idioms, 5 slang, 3 games
Reading aloud with comprehension, not decoding — the student must be able to say what it meant
Cambridge Primary Science vocabulary in English, so science class stops being a language problem
Games at warm-up, middle and finale so the hour does not sag
programmes.outcome: By the end of the year: reads a grade-level page aloud and explains it, and answers a teacher's question without translating in their head first.

programmes.name: Secondary
programmes.cadence: 2 × 60–90 min / week, plus the 45/15 at home
programmes.books: Close-up A1+ · New Close-up A2 · New Close Up B1 / B1+ · Global Success · Science
programmes.blurb: The CEFR progression the schools run — A1+ through B1+ — taught with output on top of it. The school hour is for the exam; this hour is for the student who has to hold a conversation in it.
does: Close-up and Global Success content worked through at speed, then re-used in speech
The register items: how to disagree in a meeting, how to open and close, how to refuse without apologising
Writing that is checked for argument, not just grammar
The AI-PET spaced repetition schedule — 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 days — on the vocabulary that keeps slipping
programmes.outcome: By the end of the year: a two-minute unscripted opinion, defended, with the postponing phrases gone.

programmes.name: IELTS — Grade 12 and university entry
programmes.books: IELTS materials + the student's own target band
programmes.blurb: Three years of teaching IELTS in public high schools, and the same conclusion every year: the band is lost in the speaking and writing rooms, and gained back by drills the student will actually do alone. This track is a band plan, not a textbook walk.
does: A diagnostic band sheet on day one — current band per paper, not a guess
Speaking under a timer, recorded, with the transcript written out by hand
Writing task 1 and 2 rebuilt from the band descriptors upward
Weekly listening at full speed, because the exam does not slow down
programmes.outcome: A stated target band and a dated plan to it, or the coach tells you the target is unrealistic on day one.

programmes.name: Business English & Corporate
programmes.format: In-home, at your office, or online — teams welcome
programmes.blurb: Built for the person whose English is the only thing standing between them and the contract. Meetings, negotiation, presenting, and the high-stakes small talk around all three.
does: Meeting English: opening, interrupting, redirecting, and closing with an action
Presentation rehearsal with recording, playback and a delivery score (volume, pace, eye contact)
Negotiation language and the refusal that does not damage the relationship
Email and messaging register — the difference between firm and hostile in one line
Team option: a shared block of group hours plus private sessions for the ones who need it
programmes.outcome: The next boardroom: you speak, you are understood, and you do not hand your authority to the other side.

programmes.name: The 2026 Advantage — English + AI
programmes.blurb: English alone is the old game. AI alone leaves you unable to sell what the machine produced. This track teaches the overlap: command the tool, then report on it in fluent English.
does: Prompting that gets usable work out of an AI assistant, in English
Turning machine output into a written update a manager will read
Presenting an AI-assisted result in English, including what the AI got wrong
The workflow itself: 10x output, then a fluent human report on it
programmes.outcome: You can hand in work that ten people used to do, and explain how you did it — in English.

programmes.name: Summer Intensive — Break the Chains
programmes.vn: Hè cấp tốc: Phá vỡ xiềng xích
programmes.blurb: The holiday block for the student who has studied English for years and still whispers. It is not a grammar sprint. It is a speaking project with a finish line.
does: Daily 45/15 tracked on paper — the streaks are visible to the student, not just the coach
A week-by-week output ladder: 30 seconds → 2 minutes → 5 minutes unscripted
One recorded monologue a week, played back and self-assessed against the mode ladder
The final session: a live presentation in front of someone the student did not choose
programmes.outcome: A student who stopped apologising. The Summer Intensive is the fastest route out of Mouse Mode that NET runs.

programmes.name: One-to-One, Any Age
programmes.format: In-home, online, or at your workplace
programmes.cadence: Whatever fits the week you actually have
programmes.blurb: The core NET product: one student, one coach, a plan built around the hour you actually have rather than the hour a centre would prefer to sell you. Five years of teaching in Vietnam, students from one year old to seventy.
does: A diagnostic that starts with a conversation, not a test paper
The 60% rule applied to material chosen for that student's interests
The 45/15 lifestyle integration — 45 minutes of input, 15 of output, inside a life that already exists
The 100% Confidence Guarantee: the first month, or the tuition comes back
programmes.outcome: Your own plan, your own material, your own hour. The measure is whether you open your mouth without fear.
